description: PRD-101: Mission Schema & Data Model — Full research + design PRD. Study DAG resolution, state machines, event sourcing. Design orchestration_runs, orchestration_tasks, orchestration_events tables. Define dependency resolution algorithm and state machine transitions.

userStories.title: Research DAG execution patterns
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how production DAG systems model task graphs so that our schema is informed by battle-tested patterns
acceptanceCriteria: Study Temporal workflow execution model — how it stores workflow runs, activities, and their relationships
Study Prefect flow runs — how it models task dependencies and state transitions
Study Airflow DAG runs — task instances, XCom for inter-task data, trigger rules
Study Dagster ops/jobs — asset materialization model, IO managers
Document key differences in a comparison table with columns: system, run model, task model, dependency model, state machine, failure handling
Write findings to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: DAG Execution Patterns'
Each system has at least 3 sentences of analysis, not just bullet points
Include specific schema/table examples from each system where available
userStories.notes: Use DeepWiki MCP to query these repos directly. Focus on their data models, not their execution engines — we're building our own executor. Key repos: temporalio/temporal, PrefectHQ/prefect, apache/airflow, dagster-io/dagster

userStories.title: Research state machine patterns for task lifecycle
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to understand state machine design for task lifecycle so that our status transitions are robust and well-defined
acceptanceCriteria: Define all possible task states: pending, queued, assigned, running, paused, verifying, completed, failed, cancelled, skipped
Define valid transitions between states as a transition table
Study event sourcing vs CRUD for state tracking — pros/cons for our scale
Research how Symphony handles task lifecycle (continuation vs retry distinction from PRD-100)
Document findings in PRD section: '## 3. State Machine Design'
Include ASCII state diagram showing all transitions
Address: what triggers each transition, who triggers it (coordinator, agent, human, system), what side effects occur
userStories.notes: Our existing board_tasks have simple statuses (pending, in_progress, completed, failed). The orchestration state machine needs to be richer but must MAP to board_task statuses for UI display. Read the board_tasks model in orchestrator/core/models/.

userStories.title: Design orchestration_runs table
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the orchestration_runs table designed so that every mission has a traceable execution record
acceptanceCriteria: Define orchestration_runs table with all columns, types, constraints, indexes
Required fields: id, workspace_id, title, description, goal (original user input), status enum, plan (JSONB — coordinator's decomposition), config (JSONB — autonomy level, budget, model prefs)
Tracking fields: total_cost, total_tokens, started_at, completed_at, duration_ms
Relationship fields: created_by (user_id), coordinator_agent_id (nullable — roster or system)
Foreign keys to workspaces table verified against existing schema
Include JSONB schema examples for plan and config fields
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Data Model: orchestration_runs'
Include example INSERT showing a real mission creation
Include Alembic migration pseudocode
userStories.notes: Check existing tables: workspaces, agents, board_tasks, recipes, agent_reports. The run must reference workspace_id (multi-tenant). Study how recipes store their config — similar pattern needed for mission config. Read alembic/versions/ for migration patterns used in this project.

userStories.title: Design orchestration_tasks table
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the orchestration_tasks table designed so that every subtask in a mission is tracked with dependencies
acceptanceCriteria: Define orchestration_tasks table with all columns, types, constraints, indexes
Required fields: id, run_id (FK → orchestration_runs), title, description, status enum, task_type (research, analysis, writing, coding, verification, review)
Assignment fields: agent_id (FK → agents, nullable), agent_type (roster/contractor), model_override
Dependency fields: depends_on (array of task IDs or join table), dependency_type (strict/soft)
Result fields: output (JSONB), verifier_score (float), verified_by (agent_id or 'human'), tokens_used, cost, duration_ms
Board integration: board_task_id (FK → board_tasks) — every orchestration_task creates a board_task for UI visibility
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Data Model: orchestration_tasks'
Include dependency resolution algorithm (topological sort for execution ordering)
Address: how circular dependencies are detected and rejected
userStories.notes: Critical decision: array column for depends_on vs separate orchestration_task_dependencies join table. Join table is more relational but array is simpler for our scale. Research both. The board_task_id FK is key — it's how the existing UI shows mission progress without new UI work.

userStories.title: Design orchestration_events table
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need an event log so that every state change in a mission is traceable for debugging and telemetry
acceptanceCriteria: Define orchestration_events table: id, run_id, task_id (nullable), event_type enum, payload (JSONB), created_at

Define event_type enum: run_created, run_started, task_created, task_assigned, task_started, task_completed, task_failed, task_retried, verification_passed, verification_failed, human_approved, human_rejected, budget_warning, budget_exceeded, run_completed, run_failed
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Event Log & Audit Trail'
Explain append-only design — events are never updated or deleted
Include query examples: reconstruct mission timeline, find all failures, calculate time between assignment and completion
Address retention policy — how long to keep events, archival strategy
Connect to PRD-106 (telemetry) — events are the raw data for outcome analysis
userStories.notes: This is lightweight event sourcing — we're not rebuilding state from events, we're logging them for observability. Keep it simple. The heartbeat_results JSONB in heartbeat_service already captures per-tick events — similar pattern but for missions.

userStories.title: Design integration with existing tables
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need to document how orchestration tables integrate with existing board_tasks, agents, recipes, and reports
acceptanceCriteria: Map orchestration_tasks → board_tasks: define which board_task fields are populated from orchestration_task fields
Map orchestration_runs → recipes: define 'save as routine' flow — how a completed mission becomes a recipe template
Map orchestration_tasks → agent_reports: define how task completion triggers report creation (connect to PRD-76 auto-report)
Document workspace isolation — all queries filtered by workspace_id
Write to PRD section: '## 7. Integration with Existing Schema'
Include ER diagram (ASCII or mermaid) showing relationships between all tables
List all new indexes needed for common query patterns
Address migration safety — no breaking changes to existing tables, only new tables + optional FKs
userStories.notes: Read the existing models: orchestrator/core/models/board.py, orchestrator/core/models/agent.py, orchestrator/core/models/recipe.py. Check if board_tasks already has a 'project' or 'label' field for grouping tasks under a mission. If not, that's a migration needed.

userStories.title: Write PRD introduction and problem statement
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the opening sections of PRD-101 so that readers understand the motivation and scope
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/101-MISSION-SCHEMA-DATA-MODEL.md
Section 0: Header with version, type (Research + Design), status (Draft), priority, dependencies (PRD-100)
Section 1: Problem Statement — what doesn't exist, why it's needed, what it enables
Summarize findings from US-001 through US-006 in the introduction
Include 'What This PRD Delivers' checklist — the concrete artifacts (tables, migrations, models, indexes)
Include 'What This PRD Does NOT Cover' — explicitly scope out coordinator logic, verification, budget enforcement (those are separate PRDs)
Write '## 8. Open Questions' — any unresolved design decisions that need input
userStories.notes: This is written LAST because it synthesizes all the research. Follow the style of PRD-100 — direct, honest, no marketing fluff. Include the 'We are not going blind this time' philosophy.

userStories.title: Write PRD conclusion, risks, and acceptance criteria
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to close PRD-101 with actionable acceptance criteria so that implementation PRD-82A can be written from it
acceptanceCriteria: Write '## 9. Risk Register' — at least 5 risks specific to the schema design
Write '## 10. Implementation Acceptance Criteria' — testable criteria for when the schema is 'done'
Write '## 11. Dependencies & Sequencing' — what must be built first, what can be parallel
Write '## 12. Appendix: Full SQL DDL' — complete CREATE TABLE statements ready to convert to Alembic
Write '## 13. Appendix: SQLAlchemy Models' — Python model classes matching the DDL
Final review pass — ensure all sections reference each other correctly, no dangling references
PRD-101 is complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: The SQL DDL and SQLAlchemy models are the bridge to implementation. They should be copy-pasteable into an Alembic migration and models file respectively. Use existing model patterns from orchestrator/core/models/ — same base class, same conventions.
